clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: An adult client's short peripheral IV catheter was inserted 48 hours ago. The site is nontender without erythema or warmth, and the infusion is functioning normally. Which nursing action is consistent with current CDC recommendations?

options.A: Continue the catheter, assess the insertion site daily, and remove it if phlebitis, infection, or malfunction develops.
options.B: Replace the catheter now to reduce infection risk because 48 hours is the recommended maximum dwell time for adults.
options.C: Plan routine replacement at 72 hours because that timing is the CDC standard for adult peripheral IV catheters.
options.D: Continue the catheter through completion of therapy because CDC endorses clinically indicated replacement for adults.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC recommends daily evaluation of a peripheral catheter insertion site and removal of a peripheral venous catheter when phlebitis, infection, or catheter malfunction develops. For adults, CDC states that peripheral catheters do not need routine replacement more frequently than every 72–96 hours and makes no recommendation for replacement only when clinically indicated because that remains an unresolved issue. At 48 hours with a normal, functioning site, option A is the uniquely supported action. Option B invents a 48-hour maximum dwell time. Option C converts the 72–96-hour statement into a mandatory 72-hour replacement standard. Option D treats an unresolved adult replacement strategy as a CDC recommendation.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Monitor an adult short peripheral IV site daily, remove the catheter for phlebitis, infection, or malfunction, and avoid treating clinically indicated-only replacement as an established CDC recommendation for adults.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety/Infection p.24; Pharmacological/Parenteral p.12 and p.40
audit_findings_append.finding: Original correct concept was defensible, but the correct option was uniquely long and distractors used absolute cueing. The revised item directly tests daily site assessment, complication-triggered removal, the 72–96-hour floor, and the unresolved adult clinically-indicated-only issue.

option_audit.A: Correct. Matches CDC daily site assessment and complication-triggered removal guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. CDC does not define 48 hours as the maximum adult peripheral-IV dwell time.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC does not make routine replacement at 72 hours a universal adult standard; it states there is no need to replace more frequently than every 72–96 hours.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC makes no recommendation for clinically indicated-only replacement in adults because it remains unresolved.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the relevant CDC recommendations without converting an unresolved issue into a mandate.
cueing_check: No absolute-word distractor pattern; option lengths are comparable; the correct option is not uniquely long or stylistically distinct.
